contrasts_with.desc: A discourse relation where one theory/approach is explicitly contrasted with another, often to highlight differences in assumptions, scope, or predictions. This is distinct from compares (which is about side-by-side evaluation) and claim_relation (which is about support/opposition between claims).
contrasts_with.boundary: contrasts_with = explicit opposition between two theories/approaches, NOT side-by-side evaluation (compares) and NOT support/opposition between claims (claim_relation).

validates_against.desc: A relation where a theory/model's predictions are validated or checked against experimental or observational data. This is distinct from 'compares' (which includes theory-vs-experiment as one subtype) because it specifically emphasizes the validation/evaluation aspect, not just side-by-side comparison.
validates_against.boundary: Use only when the core action is testing/evaluating a model or theory against data; not for mere side-by-side comparison or general agreement.

assesses_accuracy_of.desc: X provides means to assess/evaluate the accuracy of Y (a methodological relation where one approach serves as a benchmark or reference to evaluate another's accuracy). This is distinct from compares (which is side-by-side) and improves (which implies fixing limitations).
assesses_accuracy_of.boundary: Use when one method is explicitly used as a benchmark/reference to test another’s accuracy; not for side-by-side comparison (compares) or fixing flaws (improves).

substitutes_in.desc: A mathematical/formal relation where one operator, expression, or quantity can be substituted for another in a specific context without changing the result. This is distinct from replaces (which implies outright retirement of the old entity) and defines (which implies definitional identity).
substitutes_in.boundary: Use substitutes_in only when one thing can be swapped for another in a specific operation or proof; not for replacing/retiring (replaces) or defining equivalence (defines).

analogous_to.desc: A relation where one mathematical expression, integral, or quantity is given in a similar way to another, indicating structural or methodological analogy without implying derivation or definitional identity.
analogous_to.boundary: Use for explicit “analogous to” or “similar in form/method” comparisons; NOT for derivation, definition, or mere co-occurrence.

lacks_comparison.desc: X lacks comparison with Y, indicating that no prior work exists for comparison, highlighting novelty or absence of benchmark.
lacks_comparison.boundary: Use when explicitly stating no comparison or benchmark exists for X, not when comparing X to Y or noting a lack of evidence.

describes.desc: A relation where one entity (typically a model or theory) describes or accounts for a phenomenon or system. This is distinct from 'influences' (which implies causal dependence) and 'constitutive_law' (which requires formal quantitative relations).
describes.boundary: Applies when a model/theory explains or accounts for a phenomenon, not when it merely influences it or states a quantitative law.
